components.gap: Simon's named IP/NIP, shattering, examples and dividing-line presentation is not completed against the held October 2015 manuscript. (1) Example 2.12 (p. 17) is covered only for its first two bullets: absent are 'any theory of a pure linear order or of a pure tree, in particular T_dt, is NIP' (A.1.2), 'any C-minimal theory is NIP, the main example being ACVF' (A.1.4), 'Th(Q_p) is NIP in the pure field or the valued field language' (A.2), and the closing remark that most known NIP theories are stable or built around a linear order or a tree, with the open question whether every unstable NIP theory interprets an infinite linear order. (2) The comparisons of the introduction (pp. 8-9) that C-minimal theories are NIP and that simple and NIP theories both lie in the wider class of NTP2 theories are absent. (3) Simon's o-minimal theory in Example 2.12 has a definable total order, not necessarily dense or named by a symbol (A.1.3, p. 148: any structure on which < defines a linear order); the chapter substitutes, without saying so, def:p03-o-minimal (expansions of a dense order without endpoints, < in the language), so thm:p03-w03-p03-035-ominimal-nip proves a narrowed variant of 'any o-minimal theory is NIP' and lines 649-650 asserts that o-minimality requires the order symbol. (4) The remark after Proposition 2.8 (p. 16) that the equivalence also holds for sequences indexed by omega or by any given linear order without last element is absent. (5) Section 2.3.4 (pp. 34-36), listed by the chapter as a source, is reduced to a pointer (body 394-397): Definition 2.68 (ded), Proposition 2.69 with its written proof, the stability-function facts (polynomial bound for a stable formula at every cardinal; IP gives g(kappa) = 2^kappa for every kappa and the converse for finite kappa) and the remarks kappa < ded(kappa) <= 2^kappa and Mitchell's consistency result are not stated. (6) Narrowed variants: the paragraph after Lemma 2.7 (p. 15) bounds alternation with a finite set Delta and n on finite Delta-indiscernible sequences, while thm:p03-w03-p03-035-alternation uses full indiscernible sequences only; Example 2.4 says that in the random graph any set of elements is shattered, the chapter only finite sets; the compactness remark of p. 13 (a set is shattered iff each finite subset is) is shown only for the countable set of item (3). (7) Remark 2.2's dependent/independent terminology, Remark 2.6's pointer to Lemma 6.3 (VC*(S) < 2^(VC(S)+1) and the converse bound) and Observation 2.66 (SOP iff a definable preorder with infinite chains iff a partial order with infinite chains in T^eq) are not stated.

components.note: Formula and theory IP/NIP are defined separately; shattering, opposite-formula, indiscernible-alternation and finite type-count characterizations are proved with explicit quantifiers (sentences sigma_n, items (1)-(6), Sauer-Shelah bound, one-variable reduction). Locators checked in the held manuscript: Definition 2.1 p. 13, Lemma 2.5 p. 14, Lemma 2.7 p. 15, Propositions 2.8 and 2.11 p. 16, Lemma 6.4 p. 86.

stable implies NIP, stable implies simple (through the local dividing rank and the tree lemma) and simple plus NIP implies stable (through Theorem 2.67 and SOP excluding simplicity) are proved at theory level with written annex steps.

Random graph: IP by shattering every finite set, unstable by an explicit order-property construction, simple by the forking computation of the w03-p03-031 annex. DLO: o-minimal via order patterns, NIP, order property and SOP. RCF: o-minimal and unstable by the proved w03-p03-037 theorems, NIP and SOP here.

Remark 2.6's example (VC-dimensions 3 and 2 for x=y1 or x=y2 or x=y3 and its opposite) is asserted with a citation only (body 245-250); Simon gives no proof either.
